Sam Bankman-Fried co-founded Alameda Research in 2017 and FTX in 2019 as a complement to it. Within two years of FTX's founding, over 80 investors provided approximately $2 billion in capital. In January 2022, FTX raised $400 million in a Series C round, boosting its valuation to $32 billion. In early November 2022, CoinDesk published Alameda's balance sheet showing $14.6 billion in assets and $8 billion in liabilities as of June 30, 2022. Alameda's largest asset was $3.66 billion of 'unlocked FTT' and $2.16 billion of 'FTT collateral'. Alameda owned $5.82 billion in FTT tokens, which was 193% higher than the total FTT market cap of about $3 billion. In early November 2022, Binance pulled out its remaining $2.1 billion equivalent of cash in BUSD and FTT, triggering a bank run on FTX. FTX and Alameda filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the U.S. in mid-November 2022. Sam Bankman-Fried resigned as CEO and John J. Ray III was appointed the new CEO. SBF maintained his innocence, stating he did not try to commit fraud and was shocked by what happened. SBF was arrested in the Bahamas in December 2022, extradited to the U.S., and released on $250 million bail; his house arrest in Palo Alto was revoked in August following a diary leak accusation. During testimony, John J. Ray III stated that House Financial Services had virtually no internal controls, no separateness, and did not trust a single piece of paper; U.S. Attorney Damian Williams called the crimes the biggest financial fraud in American history. Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison pleaded guilty in December 2022 to federal charges and face civil penalties from the SEC and CFTC, planning to cooperate as witnesses. SBF pleaded not guilty in January to wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and conspiracy to misuse customer funds, facing up to 115 years in jail if convicted. The FTX collapse was the first of many, with BlockFi filing for Chapter 11 in November 2022 and Genesis Global Trading filing for Chapter 11 in January.

Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) is the disgraced cryptocurrency entrepreneur accused of orchestrating the multibillion-dollar collapse of FTX, the crypto exchange he founded and led. SBF pleaded not-guilty to some seven charges of fraud and conspiracy in Manhattan Federal Court. He reportedly offered $5 billion to Donald Trump to cancel his presidential re-run bid, though he also looked to back candidates on the Democratic side of the aisle and met with Mitch McConnell to discuss funding Republican candidates to offset Trump's influence.

SBF raised approximately $2 billion, including $1 billion in 2021, from backers that included Sequoia, Temasek, Tiger Global, and dozens more. Michael Lewis's book 'Going Infinite' is set to debut on the first day of SBF's trial; Lewis was introduced to SBF in early 2021 by a friend who wanted to back FTX, asked to meet SBF in Berkeley to 'evaluate his character,' and met SBF more than 100 times over the next two years. Lewis claimed SBF had $22.5 billion eighteen months earlier and was the richest person in the world under 30, and 60 Minutes got involved with the story, shooting a segment with SBF and Lewis.

FTX's trading volume climbed to $15 billion per day. To lend legitimacy, Tom Brady was paid $55 million and Steph Curry $35 million for marketing deals. Anna Wintour contacted SBF via Zoom to ask him to sponsor her Met Costume Ball. SBF's eyes moved back and forth during a TV appearance while trying to win a video game simultaneously.

The hard crash occurred as FTX cryptocurrency valuations fell sharply after being based on speculation rather than banked value. SBF is denied bail, blamed by crypto investors for losses at Alameda/FTX, and accused of causing a ripple effect of crypto woes. Ayelet Noff, CEO of Sliced Brand, states SBF lacked management experience, was over his head, and delayed crypto adoption by at least one to two years. Michael Lewis's interview with SBF is criticized for defending him as an 'effective altruist' and claiming FTX had a great real business, despite no proof of idealism. FTX failure resulted from financial discrepancies between the exchange and its sister company Alameda Research, a trader on the platform.

# See also

* [Sam Bankman-Fried Trial Opening Statements and Witness Testimony](sam-bankman-fried-trial-opening-statements-and-witness.md) - Details the prosecution and defense opening statements in the SBF trial, including key allegations, the defense's characterization of SBF, and the testimony of early witnesses like Marc-Antoine Julliard and Adam Yedidia.

Lewis claimed SBF had $22.5 billion eighteen months earlier and was the richest person in the world under 30, and 60 Minutes got involved with the story, shooting a segment with SBF and Lewis.

FTX's trading volume climbed to $15 billion per day. To lend legitimacy, Tom Brady was paid $55 million and Steph Curry $35 million for marketing deals. Anna Wintour contacted SBF via Zoom to ask him to sponsor her Met Costume Ball. SBF's eyes moved back and forth during a TV appearance while trying to win a video game simultaneously.

The hard crash occurred as FTX cryptocurrency valuations fell sharply after being based on speculation rather than banked value. SBF is denied bail, blamed by crypto investors for losses at Alameda/FTX, and accused of causing a ripple effect of crypto woes. Ayelet Noff, CEO of Sliced Brand, states SBF lacked management experience, was over his head, and delayed crypto adoption by at least one to two years. Michael Lewis's interview with SBF is criticized for defending him as an 'effective altruist' and claiming FTX had a great real business, despite no proof of idealism. FTX failure resulted from financial discrepancies between the exchange and its sister company Alameda Research, a trader on the platform.
